_comment: Adjudicated removals — compounds that are not physiologically active substances anyone doses, and rows that carry no pharmacology at all (a detail screen whose only content is a banner saying there is no content). Applied by SQLiteBuilder.drop_removed_substances(), which deliberately OUTRANKS the curated layer: a curated file is usually what kept an empty row alive, so removing a name here means deleting its data/curated/substances/*.json too (the build warns if one is left behind). Matching is on canonical_name only, never aliases — junk rows routinely share an alias with a legitimate one. Verdicts: not_a_substance (reagent, diagnostic analyte, cosmetic-cream ingredient, chemical-class name, protonated-cation record, vendor SKU), no_relevant_activity (real molecule, no activity a dose tracker can model), no_content (real compound, zero pharmacology in the catalog), catalog_noise (paper/patent/trial-only, never in human circulation), duplicate (supersededBy names the survivor). contentRowsAtRemoval records how many fact rows the entry held when it was cut, so a reviewer can see nothing substantial was thrown away. Each entry carries its own evidence; nothing here was removed on a hunch. A verdict that rests on a pharmacology or market claim also carries a `citation` (PMID, DOI, PubChem CID, CAS, patent or label set id) for that claim; the entries whose evidence is self-contained — the row's own emptiness, a PIHKAL commentary line, a vendor-code synonym list — are a shrink-only list in pipeline/build/tests/reason-only-baseline.json.

removed.name: 2,3-Methylenedioxyamphetamine
removed.reason: Not its own PIHKAL entry — a mention inside #100 (MDA): *"At 50 milligrams, one person was awake and alert all night, but reported no MDA-like effects."* No vendor, seizure, or trip-report footprint. A commentary mention is not the "well-known Shulgin entry" the bias rule protects.
removed.evidence: Provenance: peer-review-primary, wikidata. Evidence of human use: one Shulgin trial, 50 mg.

removed.name: 2,3-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine
removed.reason: Not in PIHKAL. And it is not an MDMA impurity — the forensic literature (e.g. Aalberg, PMID 10955507) synthesized all ten MW-193 regioisomers as standards precisely so 3,4-MDMA can be excluded from them; every mainstream route inherits the 3,4 bridge from its precursor.
removed.evidence: Provenance: peer-review-primary, wikidata. Evidence of human use: none.
